title: The fundamentals of bio-intensive market gardening on living soil
summary: Discover the pillars of bio-intensive market gardening on living soil: permanent beds, gentle overall irrigation, self-sufficient compost production and ecological intensification.

pages.title: Module overview
pages.text: Here we present the foundations of the **“bio-intensive market gardening on living soil”** method: a simple, effective approach that respects the soil, human health and the environment.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Présentation du module

pages.title: The fundamentals of bio-intensive market gardening on living soil
pages.text: This module invites you to discover and understand the core principles of **bio-intensive market gardening on living soil**, a sustainable approach to producing better while regenerating your land.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les fondamentaux du maraîchage bio-intensif en sol vivant

pages.title: What is this method?
pages.text: Let's explore together what the **bio-intensive market gardening on living soil** method involves and what benefits it brings to your crops.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Qu’est-ce que cette méthode ?

pages.title: Producing more while respecting the soil and health
pages.text:
**Bio-intensive market gardening on living soil** makes it possible to intensify production while building, season after season, a soil that is more fertile, more alive and better structured.

This method relies on simple, reproducible farming techniques that respect health and the environment.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Produire plus en respectant le sol et la santé

pages.title: Bio-intensive and living soil: the two pillars of the method
pages.text: The method draws on two complementary approaches — **living soil** and **bio-intensive** growing — which we will detail in this section.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Bio-intensif et sol vivant : les deux piliers de la méthode

pages.title: The two main pillars
pages.text:
The method rests on two main pillars:

- **Living soil**: regenerating the soil's biological life to feed plants naturally.
- **Bio-intensive growing**: producing more with less, by optimizing space and resources.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les deux grands piliers

pages.title: What is a living soil?
pages.text:
A **living soil** is a soil that is full of life: earthworms, insects, bacteria, fungi…

Together, they transform and improve the soil, enabling it to naturally nourish and strengthen plants.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Qu’est-ce qu’un sol vivant ?

pages.title: How do you build a living soil?
pages.text:
A **living soil** is built through simple but effective practices:

1. Setting up **permanent growing beds** that are never walked on.
2. **Gentle irrigation** over the whole plot.
3. **Active compost** in the pathways.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Comment construire un sol vivant ?

pages.title: The principle of bio-intensive growing
pages.text: **Bio-intensive** growing makes it possible to produce more fruits and vegetables (**intensive**) using environmentally friendly techniques (**organic**).
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Le principe du bio-intensif

pages.title: An approach based on optimization
pages.text:
Bio-intensive growing is an approach based on the **optimization** of every resource:

- Carefully calculated **plant spacing**.
- **Nurseries and transplanting** to get a head start.
- Rigorous **crop planning**.
- **Economical use and reuse** of available equipment.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Une approche basée sur l’optimisation

pages.title: A coherent whole
pages.text:
All the techniques used in the bio-intensive market gardening on living soil method complement one another.

They form a **simple and effective system**, in which each action reinforces the others.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Un tout cohérent

pages.title: The fundamentals of the method
pages.text: Let's now move on to the **four fundamental practices** that allow you to set up the method in the field and make it last.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les fondamentaux de la méthode

pages.title: The four essential practices
pages.text:
For the method to work over the long term, certain practices are essential:

1. **Permanent growing beds**.
2. Well-defined, mulched **pathways**.
3. **Compost** that is always available.
4. **Watering** of the beds and also of the pathways.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les quatre pratiques essentielles

pages.title: 1. Permanent growing beds
pages.text: The first practical pillar of the method: let's discover how **permanent growing beds** work and why they transform the plot.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 1. Les planches de culture permanentes

pages.title: Growing beds and pathways
pages.text:
The method consists of working on **permanent growing beds** that are fixed and clearly delimited.

Between the beds, there are **pathways** that let you move around without ever compacting the cultivated soil.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Planches de culture et passe-pieds

pages.title: The advantages of permanent growing beds
pages.text:
**Permanent growing beds** offer many advantages:

- **Fertile soil** is concentrated where the plants grow.
- The soil is **less compacted**.
- The soil is **protected against erosion and leaching**.
- They offer **savings in time and energy**.
- The method is **suited to small spaces**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les avantages des planches de culture permanentes

pages.title: Other ways of growing
pages.text:
We have chosen the **permanent growing bed** method, but other approaches exist:

- **Sunken beds dug into the soil**.
- **Flat-ground cultivation**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour D’autres façons de cultiver

pages.title: 2. The value of pathways
pages.text: The second essential practice: **pathways** are not just simple walkways, but a key element of garden fertility.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 2. L’intérêt des passe-pieds

pages.title: Active zones that serve fertility
pages.text:
In this market gardening method, **pathways** are not only for getting around. They are **active zones**:

- **Compost** is produced there passively through the decomposition of the mulch.
- They also help **retain moisture** across the plot.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Des zones actives au service de la fertilité

pages.title: 3. Ensuring compost availability
pages.text: The third essential practice: how to produce and maintain a sufficient supply of **compost** throughout the year.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 3. Assurer la disponibilité du compost

pages.title: Supplementing the compost from the pathways
pages.text:
The **compost** formed in the pathways is moved onto the growing beds to help soil life establish itself more quickly.

However, this production is not always enough. It is therefore important to supplement it with other inputs of **organic matter**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Compléter le compost des passe-pieds

pages.title: Making your own compost: the winter compost bin
pages.text:
To remain self-sufficient, one solution is to make your own compost.

The **winter compost bin** makes it possible to make use of materials available during the rainy season to produce quality compost at low cost.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Fabriquer son propre compost : la compostière d’hivernage

pages.title: Other composting techniques
pages.text:
Winter composting in a bin is an effective method. Other techniques exist, for example:

- **Compost pit**: a simple option when building materials are lacking.
- **Pile composting**: directly on the ground, covered to retain moisture.
- **Bokashi method**: rapid fermentation of kitchen waste, even in small quantities.
- **Surface compost**: placing materials directly on the beds to feed the soil slowly.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Autres techniques de compostage

pages.title: 4. The principle of gentle, overall irrigation
pages.text: The fourth essential practice: understanding why and how to practice **gentle, overall irrigation** across the whole garden.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour 4. Principe d’une irrigation douce et globale

pages.title: Imitating a regular, gentle rain
pages.text:
In this method, the whole plot is irrigated, including the **pathways**. Overall sprinkler irrigation can be done mechanically, with sprinkler heads, or manually with a simple watering can.

The goal is not only to water the plants, but to **keep the soil moist**. The aim is to imitate the effect of a regular, gentle rain, which nourishes soil life without disturbing it.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Imiter une pluie régulière et douce

pages.title: Other irrigation techniques
pages.text:
Other irrigation techniques exist:

- **Drip irrigation**.
- **Flood irrigation**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour D’autres techniques d’irrigation

pages.title: Beyond the fundamentals
pages.text: Once these basics are mastered, the method extends to the entire crop cycle, from sowing to harvest.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Au-delà des fondamentaux

pages.title: Summary of the method's foundations
pages.text:
We have covered the foundations of the method:

- **Permanent growing beds** with pathways.
- **Compost availability**.
- **Gentle, overall irrigation**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Récapitulatif des fondements de la méthode

pages.title: Other topics covered by the method
pages.text:
But **bio-intensive market gardening on living soil** also covers the following topics:

- **Direct sowing and transplanting**.
- **Nursery** work and production of seedlings.
- **Crop planning** and rotation.
- **Harvesting, storage** and processing of produce.
- Use of **suitable seeds**.
- **Ecological crop protection**.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Les autres sujets couverts par la méthode

pages.title: Conclusion: growing in harmony with the soil
pages.text:
**Bio-intensive market gardening on living soil** is a way of growing in harmony with the soil: a soil that we feed, that improves, and that gives back to us.

This approach makes it possible to:

- **Produce more** by growing more efficiently.
- **Be self-sufficient** in producing your own inputs.
- **Work with simple tools** that are accessible.
- **Reproduce, adapt and pass on** sustainable practices.
pages.illustration_description: Illustration pédagogique pour Conclusion : cultiver en lien avec le sol
